info.name: idempotency_lab
info.description:
Async queue idempotency lab (branch idem-api-aync-queue-flow). A Postgres-backed broker with at-least-once delivery, naive vs safe consumers, a transactional outbox relay, and chaos endpoints for redelivery and lease expiry. Every applied effect appends to audit_log, so GET /_stats shows whether a redelivery duplicated anything.

Start the lab (`make up && make run`), keep {{baseUrl}} at http://localhost:8080, then browse "1. Endpoints" by hand or run "2. Scenarios" in the Collection Runner.

item.name: Producer

request.description: Publish an order status change. Saves message_id into {{messageId}}. The safe consumer applies it only if version is higher than what is stored.
Producer-side dedupe. Same dedupe_key + same payload returns the existing message (deduped=true); same key + different payload is 422.
Publish a notification directly. Normally the outbox relay produces these from order updates.

item.description: Stand-in for an external system publishing onto the Postgres-backed broker. Topics: orders, notifications.

item.name: Consumers

request.description: Claim one order message and apply it unconditionally. Returns {"message": "no messages available"} when the topic is empty.
Claim one notification and send it unconditionally: every redelivery is a second send.
Version-guarded upsert plus an outbox_events row in the same transaction. A stale or duplicate version is skipped and acked.
Inbox pattern: INSERT INTO inbox_processed ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the same transaction as the send.
Roll back mid-transaction. The message stays leased until the lease expires (or POST /_expire_lease).
Commit the effect but skip the ack. A redelivery is then rejected by the version guard.

item.description: Claim one message per call (?topic=orders|notifications, optional ?lease_seconds=, default 5). /naive applies every delivery; /safe uses the mechanism that fits the resource.

item.name: Outbox relay

request.description: Publish up to ?limit= unpublished outbox_events rows as notifications messages, with dedupe_key outbox:{id} so a relay retry cannot double-publish.

item.description: The relay half of the transactional outbox.

item.name: Chaos (lab-only)

request.description: Reset {{messageId}} to pending regardless of status, including done -- simulates a broker replay.
Backdate the lease on {{messageId}} so the next claim can steal it, without waiting out the real lease.

item.description: Fault injection for the redelivery and stuck-lease paths.
Every route of the lab, one request each. POST /publish saves message_id into {{messageId}}, which the chaos requests use.

item.name: Check: three audit rows for one change

exec: pm.test("audit naive order.apply = 3  (one per delivery -- the bug)", () => {

item.description: At-least-once delivery means the same message can arrive again. The naive consumer applies the effect on every delivery.

item.name: 02 Version guard absorbs redelivery

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.
Simulate the broker redelivering {{messageId}} -- an ack that never reached it, or a rebalance replay.
Simulate the broker redelivering {{messageId}} -- an ack that never reached it, or a rebalance replay.

exec: pm.test("audit safe order.apply = 1  (WHERE orders.version < incoming skipped the repeats)", () => {

item.description: An order status update is naturally idempotent once it is an assignment guarded by a monotonic version. No dedup table needed: a repeat fails the guard and is acked as a no-op.

item.name: 03 Out-of-order delivery is harmless

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.

item.description: The same guard handles reordering: an older version that arrives after a newer one is skipped instead of rolling the order back.

item.name: 04 Naive notification consumer sends twice

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.
Simulate the broker redelivering {{messageId}} -- an ack that never reached it, or a rebalance replay.

exec: pm.test("audit naive notification.send = 2  (the customer got it twice)", () => {

item.description: Sending is not naturally idempotent: there is no assignment that makes sending twice equal to sending once.

item.name: 05 Inbox absorbs redelivery

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.
Simulate the broker redelivering {{messageId}} -- an ack that never reached it, or a rebalance replay.

exec: pm.test("audit safe notification.send = 1  (inbox_processed already had this message_id)", () => {

item.description: The inbox pattern: claim (consumer, message_id) with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the same transaction as the send. Zero rows inserted means already handled.

item.name: 06 Producer dedupe_key replays the same message

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.

item.description: dedupe_key is the producer-side idempotency knob (like Kafka's idempotent producer or SQS FIFO's MessageDeduplicationId), unique per (topic, dedupe_key).

item.name: 07 Same dedupe_key, different payload is rejected

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.

item.name: Reuse the key for different content

exec: pm.test("error = dedupe_key_reused_with_different_payload  (client bug, not a retry)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql("dedupe_key_reused_with_different_payload"));

item.description: The broker stores a sha256 of the canonical payload. A reused key with different content is surfaced as 422, the queue-side analogue of a mismatched HTTP fingerprint.

item.name: 08 Crash before commit: rollback, then a clean retry

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.

exec: pm.test("outbox_pending = 0  (outbox row rolled back with it)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().outbox_pending).to.eql(0));

request.description: The message is still leased by the crashed worker. Expire the lease so the next claim can take it.

exec: pm.test("audit safe order.apply = 1  (crash + retry = one apply)", () => {

item.description: The order update and its outbox row share one transaction, so a crash before COMMIT leaves no half-done state. The message stays leased; after the lease expires the retry runs cleanly.

item.name: 09 Crash after commit, before ack: redelivery is a no-op

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.
Simulate the broker redelivering {{messageId}} -- an ack that never reached it, or a rebalance replay.

item.name: Redelivery is rejected by the guard

item.description: The effect is durable but the broker never heard the ack, so it will redeliver. The version guard turns that redelivery into a no-op.

item.name: 10 Transactional outbox, end to end

request.description: Truncate every lab table so this scenario starts from zero.

exec: pm.test("outbox_pending = 1  (written in the same tx as the order update)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().outbox_pending).to.eql(1));
pm.test("published = 1  (outbox row became a notifications message)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().published).to.eql(1));
pm.test("notifications_sent = 1  (order update -> outbox -> relay -> one send)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().notifications_sent).to.eql(1));

item.description: The consumer never calls the queue directly (the dual-write problem). It writes the outbox row with the state change; the relay publishes it with dedupe_key outbox:{id}, so even a relay retry lands on the same message.

Runnable experiments, the same ten as scripts/experiments.sh. Each scenario folder starts with POST /_reset and asserts the outcome with tests, so run one scenario (or the whole folder) in the Collection Runner and read the test results.
